title: Concrete Calculator
description: Estimate how much concrete you need in cubic yards and how many bags of mix to buy.

formula.summary: Concrete volume is length × width × thickness, converted to cubic yards (the standard ready-mix ordering unit), with bag counts based on typical yield per bag size.
formula.expression: Volume (cu ft) = length × width × (thickness ÷ 12), then ÷ 27 for cubic yards

variables.meaning: Converts thickness from inches to feet
Converts cubic feet to cubic yards (27 cu ft per cu yd)

examples.title: 10ft × 10ft slab, 4 inches thick
examples.note: ≈ 1.23 cubic yards, about 56 bags of 80 lb mix

faqs.question: How much does an 80 lb bag of concrete cover?
faqs.answer: An 80 lb bag yields about 0.60 cubic feet of mixed concrete, a 60 lb bag about 0.45 cubic feet, and a 40 lb bag about 0.30 cubic feet.

faqs.question: Should I order extra concrete?
faqs.answer: Yes - most contractors add 5-10% extra to account for uneven subgrade, spillage, and form imperfections, which this calculator flags as a reminder.

faqs.question: When should I order ready-mix instead of bags?
faqs.answer: For slabs larger than roughly 1-2 cubic yards, ready-mix delivery is usually more cost-effective and less labor-intensive than mixing dozens of bags by hand.

seoContent.heading: Estimating concrete for slabs, footings, and pads
seoContent.body: Concrete is ordered by volume, typically in cubic yards for ready-mix trucks, so getting an accurate volume estimate before ordering avoids costly shortages or expensive leftover material. This calculator handles the length × width × thickness calculation and the unit conversion to cubic yards automatically.

seoContent.heading: Choosing between bagged mix and ready-mix delivery
seoContent.body: For small projects like fence post footings or a small patio, bagged concrete mix from a hardware store is often more practical. For larger slabs like driveways or garage floors, ready-mix delivery is usually cheaper per cubic yard and far less physically demanding - this calculator's cubic-yard result is exactly the number a ready-mix supplier will ask for.
